title: Strings

exercises.title: String Constants
exercises.description: Declare a string variable greeting and assign it the value "Hello, C#!". Then Console.WriteLine it using Console.WriteLine.
hints: Assign `var greeting = "…"` from a string literal.

exercises.title: Using Runes
exercises.description: Declare a rune variable and assign it the Unicode character for 'A'. Print it using both %c and %d verbs to see character vs code point.
exercises.starter_code:
char ch = 'A';
// Character / code point lines
hints: `char` holds UTF-16 code units; casting to `(int)` reveals the ordinal.
Print human-readable characters with interpolated formatting.

exercises.title: String Manipulation
exercises.description: Use strings.Contains to check if "Hello" is in "Hello, World!", strings.Replace to replace "World" with "C#", and strings.Split to split "a,b,c" by comma.
exercises.starter_code:
var text = "Hello, World!";
// Contains, Replace, Split
exercises.expected_output:
Contains: True
Replaced: Hello, Go!
First: a
hints: Use instance methods `.Contains`/`.Replace` or static `string` helpers consistently.
Split commas with `"a,b,c".Split(',')` and take index `[0]` for the first field.
When output mirrors Boolean strings, stringify with `.ToString()`.

exercises.title: String Formatting
exercises.description: Use Console.WriteLine to format a string with a name and age, then Console.WriteLine it. Also use Console.WriteLine to format a floating point number to 2 decimal places.
exercises.starter_code:
var name = "Alice"; var age = 30;
// format lines
exercises.expected_output:
Alice is 30 years old
Pi is 3.14
hints: Interpolated `$"…"` strings replace verbose composite-format calls.
`ToString("F2", CultureInfo.InvariantCulture)` pins decimal places for floating output.

exercises.title: To Upper and To Lower
exercises.description: Given s = "C# Programming", Console.WriteLine it in all uppercase and then all lowercase.
hints: Separate outputs with newline when the checker lists both forms.

exercises.title: Reverse a String
exercises.description: Given s = "hello", reverse it by converting to []rune, swapping characters, and converting back. Print the reversed string.
hints: Wrap back into `new string(chars)` for printing.

exercises.title: String HasPrefix and HasSuffix
exercises.description: Declare url = "https://example.com". Check if it starts with "https://" and ends with ".com". Print both results.
hints: Normalize boolean casing with `.ToString().ToLowerInvariant()` when grader stdout is lowercase.
